text: What is the average-case time complexity of a lookup operation in a hash table, assuming a reasonable load factor and few collisions?
explanation: Hash tables achieve O(1) average-case lookup by computing a hash of the key to jump directly to a bucket. O(log n) is characteristic of balanced binary search trees, O(n) describes the worst case for a hash table with heavy collisions (or a plain linear scan), and O(n log n) is typical of efficient comparison-based sorting, not lookup.
